intro: Lines for a live call. Every percent below is a number a publisher printed, with the dates and what it measures. Match the line to the account: default supply, aggregation price, total bill, or capacity charge. A figure with one publisher is marked single source. Where a filing printed a new rate and no publisher stated a percent, the rate is in the note and there is no percent to quote.

areas.name: Greater Toledo
areas.quote: Greater Toledo: Toledo Edison’s default price to compare was up 35% from April 2025 to April 2026.
notes: No separate Toledo-area aggregation percent turned up in the sources reviewed.

areas.name: Greater Cleveland
areas.quote: Greater Cleveland: The Illuminating Company’s default price to compare was up 37% from April 2025 to April 2026.
notes: NOPEC’s standard program price for Illuminating Company and Ohio Edison communities is 9.999¢/kWh for the June 2026 through September 2026 meter read, versus 8.999¢/kWh. Cleveland 19 (March 24, 2026) and EnergyChoiceMatters (March 19, 2026) printed the prices. Neither stated a percent.
Lorain County includes Ohio Edison accounts. Use the Ohio Edison lines on this card for those accounts.
WFMJ’s August 6, 2026 ranking for Cleveland mixes gas, electricity, and telephone. That combined percent is not quoted here.

areas.name: Columbus
areas.quote: Columbus: AEP Ohio’s price to compare jumped 36% on June 1, 2025.
notes: Upper Arlington’s SOPEC FAQ prints a June 2026 green aggregation rate of 11.162¢/kWh and a brown rate of 10.927¢/kWh, against 9.756¢/kWh through May 2026. The page does not state a percent. https://www.upperarlingtonoh.gov/m/faq?cat=48

areas.name: Cincinnati
areas.quote: Cincinnati: Duke Energy Ohio’s residential price to compare rose 30% in June 2025 and a little over 6% again in June 2026.
notes: A Duke distribution case aimed at 2027 is pending. Published descriptions of the bill impact do not agree, so no distribution percent is quoted here.

areas.name: Dayton
areas.quote: Dayton: AES Ohio’s standard-offer supply rate is up 15% for the year starting June 2026. The utility puts the typical residential bill impact at 7.5%.
notes: The City of Dayton lists the SOPEC aggregation rate at $0.0871/kWh from June 2025 to June 2026 and $0.10691/kWh from June 2026 to May 2027. The city page does not state a percent. https://www.daytonohio.gov/155/Electric-Power-Aggregation
WFMJ’s August 6, 2026 ranking for Dayton mixes gas, electricity, and telephone. That combined percent is not quoted here.

areas.name: Akron
areas.quote: Akron: Ohio Edison’s default price to compare was up 31% from April 2025 to April 2026.
notes: On March 26, 2025 the City of Akron said its Dynegy aggregation price would be 9.24¢/kWh from May 2025 through June 2026, against a prior program price of 4.97¢/kWh, and that an average residential user could expect about $40 a month more. The city did not state a percent. https://akronohio.gov/news_detail_T17_R279.php
WFMJ’s August 6, 2026 ranking for Akron mixes gas, electricity, and telephone. That combined percent is not quoted here.

areas.name: Youngstown / Warren
areas.quote: Youngstown and Warren: Ohio Edison’s price to compare was up 31% from April 2025 to April 2026. Valley electric bills were up nearly 15% over the year into July 2026.
notes: In the same August 6, 2026 WFMJ story, 10.6% is gas, electricity, and telephone together. The electric line is the nearly 15% figure.
No separate City of Youngstown aggregation percent turned up in the sources reviewed.

areas.name: Canton / Stark
areas.quote: Canton and Stark County: on Ohio Edison, the price to compare was up 31% from April 2025 to April 2026. On AEP Ohio, it jumped 36% in June 2025.
notes: Constellation’s January 22, 2025 opt-out letter for the City of Canton sets 7.965¢/kWh from March 2025 through March 2026 and names Ohio Power (AEP Ohio) as the utility. It does not state a percent change. https://www.constellation.com/content/dam/constellation/Governmental%20Aggregation/Ohio/60793-Canton-Toolkit.pdf
Stark County is split. Use the Ohio Edison lines or the AEP Ohio line according to the account.

areas.name: Ohio
areas.quote: Ohio: PJM capacity prices for 2025/26 cleared 833% above the prior delivery year. For 2026/27, PJM expects a 1.5–5% effect on some retail bills. July 2026 utility-default bills ran 12% above July 2025.
notes: PJM’s 2025 annual report prints the 2026/27 auction at $329.17/MW-day and the 2027/28 auction at the $333.44/MW-day cap. The report leaves the percent change between those two prices unstated. https://services.pjm.com/annualreport2025/markets/
Accounts outside the eight metros use this statewide card.
